answer: Model each agent as a vertex in a reputation graph where every trust thread is an edge that only forms after a small bonded deposit burns like an ember: a sybil spawns many vertices, but each new vertex must post its own bond and slowly earn incoming threads from established neighbours. Creating a hundred fake identities therefore costs a hundred bonds, while a real agent reuses one vertex and accumulates threads over time, so cheap mass identities stay isolated and untrusted while genuine work compounds.
